newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end weak, investors glued to US markets.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end weak, investors glued to US markets.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks registered their fifth consecutive losing session on Monday, succumbing to concerns about interest rates and weak U.S. markets.
The Hang Seng Index fell 84.65 points, or 0.63 percent, to 13,294.90 after dropping to a low of 13,210.59. Turnover was HK$8.61 billion, down from Friday's HK$11.12 billion.
"People are concerned about the U.S. markets in general," said Henry Lui, research analyst at Mansion House Research.
"Investors seem to be a little bit bearish about the Dow Jones in the short term which has triggered the local market to fall," he said.
With the U.S. Federal Reserve's next policy setting meeting coming up on February 4-5, analysts said market tone may remain cautious, with the Hang Seng trapped in a range.
A rising U.S. long bond yield was the cause of some concern and continued weakness in the Dow was likely to hurt market sentiment, they said.
The U.S. long bond fell 12/32 to yield 6.89 percent on Friday and the Dow industrials dropped 59.27 points to 6,696.48.
"Overseas markets are under consolidation and at the moment we are seeing no additional flows of funds into the market," said Edwin Cheung, dealing director at Taiwan Securities.
But analysts said the Hang Seng may have found strong support at 13,200 points.
"It looks like temporarily we have seen a low there and it looks like we will see a rebound tomorrow," said Dharmala Securities technical analyst Alex Wong.
"We might see some kind of move take place but we need to clear above resistance at 13,600 points to confirm that the recent correction has ended," he added.

Giordano tumbled HK$1.25 to HK$3.80. The clothing retailer said negotiations regarding new outlets in Beijing and Shanghai had not been concluded and it was continuing to address regulatory procedural demands concerning its China operations.
Conglomerates took a hit on Monday, with Hutchison down HK$1.50 at HK$59.75 and Swire falling HK$1.75 to HK$72.00.
In the banking sector, HSBC fell HK$2.00 to HK$175.50 and Bank of East Asia fell HK$0.30 to HK$35.20.
But China Light and Power rose HK$0.60 to HK$33.70. Red chips moved ahead with CITIC Pacific up HK$1.10 at HK$39.50 and Shanghai Industrial up HK$0.75 to HK$27.85.
January Hang Seng Index futures, which expire on Thursday, closed 60 points lower at 13,205.
